entries: **The app told Homebrew users to run a command that cannot work.** With no status file on disk, the popover footer said `Run python3 main.py --setup and open Claude Code once` — an instruction written for people who cloned the repo. Someone who installed the cask has no repo, so the natural next move is to look inside the bundle, and `main.py` really is in there: py2app copies it to `Contents/Resources/`. Running that copy with the system `python3` dies on `ImportError: cannot import name 'packaged_resource_path' from 'i18n'`, which points at the wrong thing entirely. The modules `main.py` imports are compiled into `lib/python313.zip`, and only the bundle's own interpreter has that on `sys.path`; with the real `i18n.py` unreachable, an unrelated PyPI package also named `i18n` in the user's site-packages answers the import instead. Both footer messages now name the "Set Up Status Line" button, which does the same job in one click and exists in every install regardless of how it was obtained. entries: **The panel window oscillated between two heights.** Opening it snapped the window once, and it kept flicking back and forth afterwards. A panel's height has two sources: `popover_dimensions()` estimates it in Python from a registered base plus per-card adjustments, and the page measures itself for real once it has been laid out and reports the number back. The measurement is meant to win — it is saved to `NSUserDefaults` and read back by `resolve_panel_size()` on the next pass. It never was. `NSUserDefaults.objectForKey_()` hands PyObjC an Objective-C `__NSDictionaryI`, and `isinstance(value, dict)` on that is `False`, so the guard rejected the saved `{classic: 974}` every single time and fell back to the 1004 estimate. The write path had the same guard and therefore discarded every other panel's saved height whenever one was stored. What made this hard to see is that saving worked while loading did not: `defaults read com.lollapalooza.usage` showed the correct 974 sitting on disk the whole time, so the data looked healthy from the outside. The 30-point gap between the two values happens to equal `status_wrap_extra_height`, which is a coincidence worth ignoring — the estimate being wrong is not what caused the loop; the measurement being rejected is. Both guards now accept `collections.abc.Mapping`. The estimate is still used, but only for panels that can never report a measurement — `ErrorPanelView` has no JavaScript bridge, so waiting for one would leave it at the wrong size forever. The regression test substitutes a `MappingProxyType`, which like `NSDictionary` is a `Mapping` that is not a `dict`; a test double built from a plain `dict` passes whether or not the bug is present.

**The Japanese and Korean locales shipped sixty-three blank labels each.** Flagged one version earlier and fixed here. Both locales carried all 489 keys, so `test_every_language_has_the_same_keys` compared key sets, found them identical, and passed — while `loading`, `no_data`, `session_title`, `col_time` and `model_breakdown` rendered as empty space for anyone running the app in either language. A present-but-empty value is invisible to a parity check by construction, which is the same blind spot that let fifty-two Simplified Chinese strings sit in the Traditional Chinese locale until last version. Two assertions now close it: no translated value may be blank, and every value's `{placeholder}` set must match English exactly. The second guards a failure the first cannot see — a translation that drops or renames a placeholder does not look wrong in the file, it raises at `format` time in front of the user. Rich markup (`[dim]`), format specs (`{m:02d}`) and command names were left in English.

title.en: Panel windows stop flickering between heights

entries: **The offline price table overcharged Opus 4.6 and 4.7 threefold, and valued Opus 5 at nothing.** `_fallback_pricing()` is what the cost estimate falls back on when the LiteLLM table cannot be downloaded or its cache has expired. It is written by hand and nothing ever reconciled it against the live table, so it drifted in silence: `claude-opus-4-6` and `claude-opus-4-7` still carried the Opus 4.1-era $15/$75 per Mtok long after Anthropic dropped Opus to $5/$25, `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` was twenty percent low, and `claude-opus-5` was missing outright — and a missing key makes `calculate_cost()` return `0.0`, so Opus 5 usage was reported as costing nothing. The corrected figures come from reconciling against the cached LiteLLM table rather than from the changelog: Claude Code 2.1.219 announced Opus 5 at `$10/$50 per Mtok`, but that is the fast-mode price, not the standard one. What makes this class of bug worth naming is when it surfaces — only offline, which is exactly the moment nobody thinks to doubt the number on screen.

**Fifty-two keys in the Traditional Chinese locale contained Simplified Chinese.** The TUI and report strings had been copied across from `zh-CN` without conversion, so a Traditional Chinese user opening the TUI read `检测到`, `时间`, `来源`, `项目` and `消息`. A hand-written list of Simplified characters found only some of them — it missed `来` and `项` — so every value was instead run through OpenCC's `s2twp` and the differences reviewed one by one. Nine of those differences were the converter overreaching on text that was already correct (`發送`→`傳送`, `吹回`→`吹迴`, `連接詞`→`連線詞`) and were left alone. The golden HTML snapshot was patched for the two strings that actually changed rather than regenerated, because regenerating it would also replace the frozen timestamp and version the test asserts on. The same region of `ja` and `ko` holds sixty-three empty strings each; those are missing translations rather than wrong ones and are left for a separate change.

**`_refresh_in_background` moved into `menubar_refresh.py`.** At 203 lines it was the largest method in `menubar.py`, which had four lines left under its ceiling — and a ceiling exists on that file precisely because it has been split apart and grown back twice. Only three lines of the method touch PyObjC, the three `performSelectorOnMainThread` calls, and those stay behind along with every selector: an AppDelegate method is bound by name, so relocating one breaks the binding. What moved is the data work between them, split into `load_sources()` and `build_result()`, with the app passed in behind a `typing.Protocol` so the new module imports no PyObjC at all — the same rule that keeps `menubar_state.py` clean. `menubar.py` goes from 2116 lines to 1934 and the ceiling was lowered to match rather than raised, since raising it to get CI green would dismantle the only thing stopping the file from growing back a third time. Behaviour is unchanged, and that was verified rather than assumed: the six `refresh_timing` stages, the fifteen state assignments on the degraded path, and the `submitted`/`finally` guard that keeps a failed refresh from wedging the app were each compared line by line against the original.

title.en: Cost estimates stay accurate when you're offline

body.en: When you are away from the internet and checking what your usage cost, the number on screen needs to be dependable. It was not: Opus 4.6 and 4.7 were priced at three times their rate, while Opus 5 appeared to cost nothing. If LiteLLM's price table could not be downloaded, or its cache (saved lookup results kept for reuse) had expired, the app used a hand-maintained fallback table that had drifted from the current one. It is now reconciled with LiteLLM's cached table: 4.6 and 4.7 move from $15/$75 to $5/$25 per million billing units, Haiku 4.5 regains its missing twenty percent, and Opus 5 no longer returns $0. Think of an offline checkout pulling out an old price sheet; it now has the right sheet when you need it most.

title.en: Menu-bar refresh work moves house without changing behavior

body.zh-TW: 你會看到選單列照常更新，只是背後那段 203 行的工作搬了家。`menubar.py` 已經拆過又長回來兩次，原先離檔案長度上限只差四行；與其把上限往上推，開發者把背景更新的資料處理拆到 `menubar_refresh.py`，分成 `load_sources()` 和 `build_result()`。畫面相關的三次 `performSelectorOnMainThread` 呼叫與所有 selector（靠名稱找到要執行方法的標記）留在原檔，因為 AppDelegate 的方法就是按名稱綁定，搬走會斷線。新檔透過 `typing.Protocol` 描述需要的 App 介面，完全不載入 PyObjC。像把塞爆的廚房分出備料間：接客的窗口不動，備料移到隔壁，送餐流程仍照原本走。六個更新計時階段、降級路徑的 15 次狀態寫入，以及失敗後避免卡死的保護，都逐行比對確認沒變。

entries: **The file log is bounded and rotates.** The only log on disk was whatever launchd redirected into `~/Library/Logs/usage/usage.log`, and a redirect has no size limit — for a menu bar app that stays open for months, that file only ever grows. Python now owns a log of its own beside it, capped at 2 MB with three archives kept. Building the handler is best-effort: if the directory cannot be created the app keeps its console output and starts normally, because a logging subsystem must never be the thing that stops the program from running. macOS keeps the `~/Library/Logs/usage/` convention; every other platform writes under `~/.usage/logs/` next to the disk caches, since `~/Library/Logs` means nothing on Windows and `_setup_logging()` runs before the platform branch.

**`USAGE_DEBUG` selects subsystems instead of switching everything on.** It was a boolean, so diagnosing one loader meant turning on all forty-odd debug sites and reading the result through the noise. It now takes a comma-separated list — `USAGE_DEBUG=codex_loader,pricing` raises only those two. Prefix matching comes free from Python's logger hierarchy rather than a hand-written comparison: setting `a.b` covers `a.b.c` because that is how logger inheritance already works. `1`, `all` and `*` keep the previous global behaviour.

**`--doctor --json` emits the report as data with stable codes.** The report was a block of text, so a user could only screenshot it and the reader had to scan by eye — nothing could compare two reports or decide programmatically which check failed. Each check now carries a fixed code (`hook_state`, `codex_sessions`, …) and one of three states, the process exits non-zero when any check is in error, and the human-readable output is unchanged to the character. Ambiguous cases resolve to `warn` rather than `error`: a false alarm that fails a health check costs more than a missed warning.

**The test suite wrote into the developer's real log file.** `tests/test_main.py` exercises `main()`, whose first action is `_setup_logging()` — so the run attached a rotating file handler pointed at the actual `~/Library/Logs/usage/usage-app.log`, and every warning logged by every later test landed in it. One full run deposited 8 KB containing pytest's temporary directory paths, which is worse than noise: it makes the log untrustworthy the day someone reads it for a real diagnosis. An autouse fixture now redirects the log directory to `tmp_path`, matching the existing rule for `cache_quarantine.QUARANTINE_DIR`. Curiously the same class of bug was fixed one version earlier in the Windows tray tests.

**`switchPanel_` builds its items through a helper.** A dozen menu entries each repeated the same five to seven lines — allocate the item, set the target, set the state, set the tooltip, add it — and `menubar.py` had two lines left under its ceiling. `menubar_menu.build_menu_item()` absorbs that shape. It lives in a new module rather than in `menubar_state.py`, which stays free of PyObjC. `switchPanel_` itself does not move: an AppDelegate method is bound by selector, and relocating one breaks the binding. The saving is smaller than it looks — 24 lines, not the 80 the line count suggested, because keyword arguments wrap across lines and give much of it back. The gain is the removed repetition, not the arithmetic. Moving the helper out also broke a test that patched `NSMenuItem` on the `menubar` module only; the fix was to patch the helper module too, never to add module-level indirection so the old patch keeps reaching.

title.zh-TW: 日誌會輪替，測試也不再污染真實紀錄
title.en: Logs now rotate, and tests stop polluting the real record

body.zh-TW: 電腦常駐幾個月時，日誌檔（log，記錄程式運作過程的文字檔）若只由 launchd 轉存，就會像永遠不換頁的筆記本，只增不減。這個選單列小程式原本由 launchd 轉存輸出到 `~/Library/Logs/usage/usage.log`，沒有大小限制。launchd（macOS 用來在背景啟動程式的服務）只負責轉送。現在 Usage 在旁邊自己管理日誌：每份最多 2 MB，保留三份舊檔；就算建立目錄失敗，也照常啟動並保留主控台輸出。macOS 寫進 `~/Library/Logs/usage/`，其他平台則寫 `~/.usage/logs/`。連測試也改把日誌導去暫存目錄，不會再把測試警告混進真正用來診斷的 `usage-app.log`；Windows 系統匣測試曾在前一版修過同類問題。
body.en: When a computer stays on for months, a log file can become a notebook that never turns a page: it only grows. launchd, macOS's background service launcher, had been redirecting output to `~/Library/Logs/usage/usage.log` with no size limit. Usage now manages its own nearby log: each file is capped at 2 MB and three old copies are retained; even if it cannot create the directory, the app still starts and keeps console output. macOS uses `~/Library/Logs/usage/`; other platforms use `~/.usage/logs/`. Tests now write logs to a temporary directory too, so their warnings no longer mingle with the real `usage-app.log` used for diagnosis.

items.original:
**The file log is bounded and rotates.** The only log on disk was whatever launchd redirected into `~/Library/Logs/usage/usage.log`, and a redirect has no size limit — for a menu bar app that stays open for months, that file only ever grows. Python now owns a log of its own beside it, capped at 2 MB with three archives kept. Building the handler is best-effort: if the directory cannot be created the app keeps its console output and starts normally, because a logging subsystem must never be the thing that stops the program from running. macOS keeps the `~/Library/Logs/usage/` convention; every other platform writes under `~/.usage/logs/` next to the disk caches, since `~/Library/Logs` means nothing on Windows and `_setup_logging()` runs before the platform branch.
**The test suite wrote into the developer's real log file.** `tests/test_main.py` exercises `main()`, whose first action is `_setup_logging()` — so the run attached a rotating file handler pointed at the actual `~/Library/Logs/usage/usage-app.log`, and every warning logged by every later test landed in it. One full run deposited 8 KB containing pytest's temporary directory paths, which is worse than noise: it makes the log untrustworthy the day someone reads it for a real diagnosis. An autouse fixture now redirects the log directory to `tmp_path`, matching the existing rule for `cache_quarantine.QUARANTINE_DIR`. Curiously the same class of bug was fixed one version earlier in the Windows tray tests.

title.zh-TW: 除錯可只看指定區塊，不必淹沒所有訊息
title.en: Debugging can now target selected parts instead of flooding everything

body.zh-TW: 想查價格載入出了什麼事，卻被四十多處 debug 輸出淹沒嗎？USAGE_DEBUG（除錯開關，用來要求程式多印診斷訊息）不再只是全開或全關。在啟動前的環境變數（給程式的外部設定值）填 `USAGE_DEBUG=codex_loader,pricing`，就只看這兩個子系統；填 `1`、`all` 或 `*`，仍維持原本全部開啟。若填 `a.b`，它也會涵蓋 `a.b.c`，因為 Python 的 logger hierarchy（記錄器會由上層名稱管到下層名稱的結構）本來就這樣繼承。像開演唱會的控台，現在可只打亮兩位表演者，不必把整座舞台的燈全開。
body.en: Trying to find out why pricing loaded oddly used to mean drowning in output from more than forty debug sites. `USAGE_DEBUG`, the switch that asks the program to print diagnostic messages, is no longer only all on or all off. Set the environment variable before launch to `USAGE_DEBUG=codex_loader,pricing` and only those two subsystems speak up; `1`, `all`, and `*` still enable everything. Setting `a.b` also covers `a.b.c`, because Python's logger hierarchy already passes settings from a parent name to its children. It is like a concert board that can light only two performers instead of every lamp on the stage.

items.original: **`USAGE_DEBUG` selects subsystems instead of switching everything on.** It was a boolean, so diagnosing one loader meant turning on all forty-odd debug sites and reading the result through the noise. It now takes a comma-separated list — `USAGE_DEBUG=codex_loader,pricing` raises only those two. Prefix matching comes free from Python's logger hierarchy rather than a hand-written comparison: setting `a.b` covers `a.b.c` because that is how logger inheritance already works. `1`, `all` and `*` keep the previous global behaviour.

title.zh-TW: 健康檢查可交給程式比對，不只剩截圖
title.en: Health checks can now be compared by programs, not just screenshots

body.zh-TW: 有人請你交出 Usage 的健康檢查結果時，`usage --doctor --json` 現在給的是可讀取的資料，而不只是一段得靠截圖保存的文字。每項檢查都有固定代碼（stable code，讓程式每次都能辨認同一項檢查的名稱），例如 `hook_state`、`codex_sessions`，並標成三種狀態；只要有 `error`，指令就用非零結束碼（告訴其他程式這次執行失敗的數字）結束，其他工具便能比較兩次結果或自動判斷哪項失敗。邊界不清時它選 `warn`，不誤報成 `error`。像健檢表換上固定欄位，電腦和人都能對照。
body.en: When someone asks for Usage's health-check result, `usage --doctor --json` now returns data a program can read rather than a block of text that needs a screenshot. Each check has a stable code, such as `hook_state` or `codex_sessions`, and one of three states. If any check is an `error`, the command ends with a non-zero exit code, so other tools can compare two reports or determine which check failed automatically. When the boundary is unclear, it chooses `warn` instead of falsely calling it an `error`. It is like a medical form with fixed columns: people and computers can both line up the results.

items.original: **`--doctor --json` emits the report as data with stable codes.** The report was a block of text, so a user could only screenshot it and the reader had to scan by eye — nothing could compare two reports or decide programmatically which check failed. Each check now carries a fixed code (`hook_state`, `codex_sessions`, …) and one of three states, the process exits non-zero when any check is in error, and the human-readable output is unchanged to the character. Ambiguous cases resolve to `warn` rather than `error`: a false alarm that fails a health check costs more than a missed warning.

title.zh-TW: 選單項目集中組裝，綁定的方法仍留在原地
title.en: Menu items are assembled in one place while the bound method stays put

body.zh-TW: 維護 macOS 選單列時，麻煩的往往不是加新選項，而是十幾個選項都重複同一套組裝動作。`switchPanel_` 現在交給 `menubar_menu.build_menu_item()` 幫手函式（helper function，把重複步驟集中在一處的小函式）建立項目，建立項目、設定目標、狀態、提示，再加入選單的步驟只寫一次。`switchPanel_` 本身沒有搬家，因為 AppDelegate（macOS 應用程式的協調者）會用 selector 綁定它。selector（依方法名稱連接功能的機制）若失去原方法就會斷掉。這次省下的是 24 行重複內容，不是看起來像 80 行的數字遊戲；舊測試也改為在幫手模組補上 `NSMenuItem` 的替換，不再加模組層級轉接。像把十幾張便條收進同一本簿子，項目仍在原處，只有抄寫不再重複。
body.en: When maintaining a macOS menu bar, the trouble is often not adding a new option but repeating the same assembly steps for a dozen of them. `switchPanel_` now uses `menubar_menu.build_menu_item()`, a helper function that gathers repeated steps in one place, to create the items; target, state, tooltip, and adding the item are written once. `switchPanel_` itself stays where it is because AppDelegate binds it through a selector, the mechanism that connects a feature by method name. Move the original method and that connection breaks. This removes 24 repeated lines, not the 80-line illusion suggested by the count. The old test now also replaces `NSMenuItem` in the helper module instead of adding module-level indirection. It is like gathering a dozen sticky notes into one notebook: the items stay put, but copying stops repeating.

items.original: **`switchPanel_` builds its items through a helper.** A dozen menu entries each repeated the same five to seven lines — allocate the item, set the target, set the state, set the tooltip, add it — and `menubar.py` had two lines left under its ceiling. `menubar_menu.build_menu_item()` absorbs that shape. It lives in a new module rather than in `menubar_state.py`, which stays free of PyObjC. `switchPanel_` itself does not move: an AppDelegate method is bound by selector, and relocating one breaks the binding. The saving is smaller than it looks — 24 lines, not the 80 the line count suggested, because keyword arguments wrap across lines and give much of it back. The gain is the removed repetition, not the arithmetic. Moving the helper out also broke a test that patched `NSMenuItem` on the `menubar` module only; the fix was to patch the helper module too, never to add module-level indirection so the old patch keeps reaching.

entries: **Token estimates no longer undercount CJK text by a factor of four.** Six places in the waste diagnosis converted characters to tokens with `chars // 4`, which is the ASCII ratio. A CJK character is roughly one token, not a quarter of one, so every figure the diagnosis reported for a Chinese, Japanese or Korean file — wasted tokens and the cost derived from them — came out at a quarter of the truth. This project reads its own `i18n.json`, `CLAUDE.md` and `README.zh-TW.md` often enough to hit this on itself. The estimate now counts CJK codepoints as one token each and everything else at four characters per token. No tokenizer dependency was added: this is an offline tool, and pulling in a model-specific tokenizer to chase rounding-level accuracy is not a trade worth making.

**A corrupt disk cache is preserved instead of being deleted outright.** All three caches — Antigravity, Codex and history — dealt with an unreadable file by removing it and recomputing. That is the right recovery, but it also destroys the only evidence of what went wrong, so a later report of "my numbers look off" has nothing left to inspect. A damaged file is now moved to `~/.usage/quarantine/` first, named with a millisecond timestamp so a second failure cannot overwrite the first, capped at ten files and 5 MB each. A stale `schema_version` is *not* quarantined: that is an ordinary upgrade, and with 32 shards per cache one version bump would flush the whole budget and push the real evidence out. The quarantine helper swallows every error it can hit — it is a side service and must never take the caller down with it.

**`--doctor` no longer reports a missing file that the current mode does not use.** The report listed fourteen checks as one flat list, so `forwarder script: [missing]` read as a fault even when the installed mode never needs that script. It is now grouped into `[core]`, `[hook]` and `[optional]`, and the forwarder line says `[not needed in <state> mode]` when that is the case. None of the check logic changed.

**Two Windows tray tests wrote into the real `~/.claude/usage-preferences.json`.** Both call `switch_panel()`, which persists through `_save_active_panel_id()`, and neither patched `prefs.PREFERENCES_FILE` — so running the suite silently changed the developer's own active panel.

**The documentation parity check covers Simplified Chinese, Japanese and Korean.** `check_doc_parity.py` only compared English against Traditional Chinese, leaving the other three README translations unwatched; `CLAUDE.md` had to carry a note to sync them by hand. Each translation is now compared on its own and the failure message names the file that drifted. The comparison is still a count of `##` headings rather than their text — matching text would force translators to mirror English headings word for word, which is what makes translated docs read badly.

**`scripts/install_local.sh` replaces the hand-typed steps for installing a build locally.** Releasing does not touch `/Applications`: the tag drives CI, and the local copy keeps running whatever was already there. That last step lived only in a checklist, and the menu bar once ran a stale build for six versions before anyone noticed. The script checks the build exists, prints both versions, waits for the running app to exit, swaps it, and verifies the installed version matches.

title.zh-TW: 中文、日文、韓文的用量估算不再少算四倍
title.en: Usage estimates no longer count CJK text at one quarter of its size

body.zh-TW: 你拿中文、日文或韓文檔案檢查浪費的用量時，以前看到的數字其實少算了四倍。診斷工具把所有文字都當成四個字元才算一個 token（AI 處理文字量的單位），這套演算法適合 ASCII 文字，卻不適合 CJK 文字：一個中日韓字大約就是一個 token。現在它會把中日韓字逐一計算，其餘文字仍以四個字元估算，所以浪費的 token 與由此算出的費用不會再縮成四分之一。這像秤蔬菜時把每四顆番茄才當一顆，秤重結果當然偏低；秤法改正後，數字才接近實際重量。工具仍在離線運作，沒有為了追求細微的取整誤差加入特定模型的 tokenizer。
body.en: If you use Chinese, Japanese, or Korean files to diagnose waste, the old figures were four times too small. The diagnostic treated every four characters as one token (the unit an AI uses to measure text). That works for ASCII text, but a CJK character is roughly one token. It now counts each CJK codepoint as one token and keeps the four-characters-per-token estimate for everything else, so reported waste and the cost based on it no longer shrink to a quarter of their real estimate. It was like weighing tomatoes but recording only one for every four on the scale. The tool remains offline; it does not add a model-specific tokenizer just to chase tiny rounding differences.

items.original: **Token estimates no longer undercount CJK text by a factor of four.** Six places in the waste diagnosis converted characters to tokens with `chars // 4`, which is the ASCII ratio. A CJK character is roughly one token, not a quarter of one, so every figure the diagnosis reported for a Chinese, Japanese or Korean file — wasted tokens and the cost derived from them — came out at a quarter of the truth. This project reads its own `i18n.json`, `CLAUDE.md` and `README.zh-TW.md` often enough to hit this on itself. The estimate now counts CJK codepoints as one token each and everything else at four characters per token. No tokenizer dependency was added: this is an offline tool, and pulling in a model-specific tokenizer to chase rounding-level accuracy is not a trade worth making.

title.zh-TW: 壞掉的快取先隔離，留下查問題的線索
title.en: A damaged cache is quarantined instead of erased

body.zh-TW: 某次用量數字看起來不對時，壞掉的快取（把查過結果暫存起來直接用的資料）現在不會立刻被刪光。Antigravity、Codex 與 history 三種快取遇到讀不懂的檔案，仍會重新計算以便繼續使用，但會先把原檔移到 `~/.usage/quarantine/`，讓你日後還能檢查出了什麼問題。每個檔名帶毫秒時間戳，第二次故障不會蓋掉第一次；隔離區最多留十個檔案，每個最多 5 MB。這像醫院把破損的檢體先放進證物袋，再重新採樣，而不是直接丟進垃圾桶。只有過期的 `schema_version` 不會被隔離，因為那是正常升級；每個快取有 32 個分片，一次升版若全送進隔離區，反而會擠掉真正的故障證據。
body.en: When a usage number looks wrong, a damaged cache (stored results reused instead of recomputed) will no longer vanish immediately. Antigravity, Codex, and history caches still recover by recomputing an unreadable file, but first move the original into `~/.usage/quarantine/` so there is something to inspect later. Names include a millisecond timestamp, so a second failure cannot replace the first; the folder holds at most ten files, up to 5 MB each. It is like bagging a damaged lab sample before taking a new one instead of throwing away the only clue. An old `schema_version` is excluded because it is a normal upgrade. With 32 shards per cache, quarantining an entire version bump would crowd out the evidence from a real failure.

items.original: **A corrupt disk cache is preserved instead of being deleted outright.** All three caches — Antigravity, Codex and history — dealt with an unreadable file by removing it and recomputing. That is the right recovery, but it also destroys the only evidence of what went wrong, so a later report of "my numbers look off" has nothing left to inspect. A damaged file is now moved to `~/.usage/quarantine/` first, named with a millisecond timestamp so a second failure cannot overwrite the first, capped at ten files and 5 MB each. A stale `schema_version` is *not* quarantined: that is an ordinary upgrade, and with 32 shards per cache one version bump would flush the whole budget and push the real evidence out. The quarantine helper swallows every error it can hit — it is a side service and must never take the caller down with it.

title.zh-TW: `--doctor` 會分清楚「缺檔」與「根本用不到」
title.en: `--doctor` separates a missing file from one you do not need

body.zh-TW: 跑 `--doctor` 檢查安裝狀態時，看到 `forwarder script: [missing]` 不必再先以為出錯。以前報告把十四項檢查攤成一張清單，即使你目前的模式根本不用 forwarder script（負責轉送資料的腳本），它也照樣標成 missing。現在結果分成 `[core]`、`[hook]` 與 `[optional]` 三組；不需要轉送腳本的模式會直接寫 `[not needed in <state> mode]`。這像健康檢查把必做檢驗、加選檢驗和不適用項目分欄，而不是把所有未做項目都標紅。檢查的判斷規則沒有改，改的是報告把情境講清楚的方式；真正缺少目前模式會用到的檔案，仍會顯示為問題。
body.en: When you run `--doctor` to check an installation, `forwarder script: [missing]` no longer automatically means trouble. The report used to flatten fourteen checks into one list, so it showed a missing forwarder script even in a mode that never uses one. A forwarder script is simply a script that passes data along. Results are now separated into `[core]`, `[hook]`, and `[optional]`; a mode that does not need the script says `[not needed in <state> mode]`. It is like a health report separating required tests, elective tests, and tests that do not apply instead of marking every absent test red. The checking logic itself did not change; a file required by the current mode is still reported as missing.

items.original: **`--doctor` no longer reports a missing file that the current mode does not use.** The report listed fourteen checks as one flat list, so `forwarder script: [missing]` read as a fault even when the installed mode never needs that script. It is now grouped into `[core]`, `[hook]` and `[optional]`, and the forwarder line says `[not needed in <state> mode]` when that is the case. None of the check logic changed.

title.zh-TW: Windows 的系統匣測試會寫入真實偏好設定
title.en: Windows tray tests write to your real preferences

body.zh-TW: Windows 開發者跑系統匣（Windows 工作列角落放背景程式圖示的區域）測試後，自己的面板偏好曾被悄悄改掉。兩個測試都會呼叫 `switch_panel()` 切換面板；這個動作接著透過 `_save_active_panel_id()` 寫入偏好檔，但測試沒有把 `prefs.PREFERENCES_FILE` 改指向暫存位置，於是實際碰到的是 `~/.claude/usage-preferences.json`。換句話說，測試本來該在模型屋裡搬家具，卻走進你的家改了客廳。
body.en: After a Windows developer ran tray tests, their own panel preference changed in silence. The tray is the corner of the Windows taskbar where background-app icons live. Two tests call `switch_panel()`, which then writes preferences through `_save_active_panel_id()`. But the tests did not redirect `prefs.PREFERENCES_FILE` to a temporary location, so they wrote to the real `~/.claude/usage-preferences.json`. The tests were meant to rearrange furniture in a model home, yet walked into your living room instead.

items.original: **Two Windows tray tests wrote into the real `~/.claude/usage-preferences.json`.** Both call `switch_panel()`, which persists through `_save_active_panel_id()`, and neither patched `prefs.PREFERENCES_FILE` — so running the suite silently changed the developer's own active panel.

title.zh-TW: 四種 README 翻譯都有人守，不再只盯繁中
title.en: Documentation checks now watch all four README translations

body.zh-TW: 英文 README 多加一節時，簡體中文、日文和韓文版現在也會被檢查有沒有跟上。原本 `check_doc_parity.py` 只比對英文與繁中 README，其他三份翻譯沒有自動守門員，只能靠 `CLAUDE.md` 裡的手動提醒。現在每一種翻譯各自和英文比較，若落後，錯誤訊息會直接點出是哪個檔案。它比的是 `##` 標題的數量，不是標題文字本身：譯者仍可用自然的語言改寫標題，不必逐字照翻。這像展覽入口只數每個語言版有沒有同樣多扇展廳門，而不強迫門牌翻成同一串字；少了一扇門才提醒你回頭補。
body.en: When the English README gains a section, the Simplified Chinese, Japanese, and Korean versions are now checked for keeping up too. `check_doc_parity.py` used to compare English only with Traditional Chinese, leaving the other three translations guarded only by a hand-written reminder in `CLAUDE.md`. Each translation is now compared with English on its own, and a failure names the file that drifted. The check counts `##` headings rather than matching their wording, so translators can still write natural headings instead of copying English word for word. It is like checking that every language edition of an exhibition has the same number of gallery doors, without forcing all the signs to use identical words.

items.original: **The documentation parity check covers Simplified Chinese, Japanese and Korean.** `check_doc_parity.py` only compared English against Traditional Chinese, leaving the other three README translations unwatched; `CLAUDE.md` had to carry a note to sync them by hand. Each translation is now compared on its own and the failure message names the file that drifted. The comparison is still a count of `##` headings rather than their text — matching text would force translators to mirror English headings word for word, which is what makes translated docs read badly.

title.zh-TW: 本機安裝有了腳本，選單列不再默默跑舊版
title.en: A local-install script keeps the menu bar from quietly running an old build

body.zh-TW: 你剛做完本機 build（編譯完成、可執行的程式版本），標上 release tag 並不會自動換掉 `/Applications` 裡正在跑的 App。過去這一步只寫在檢查清單，曾讓選單列連續六個版本仍開著舊 build。現在要在本機安裝時，直接執行 `scripts/install_local.sh`：它先確認 build 存在，印出新舊兩個版本，等待正在執行的 App 結束，再替換檔案，最後核對已安裝版本是否相同。這像買了新燈泡卻只把盒子放在門口；打上標籤不等於已裝進燈座。腳本把拆舊燈、裝新燈和開燈確認串起來，讓本機副本跟著更新。
body.en: After you make a local build (a compiled, runnable version of the app), adding a release tag does not replace the copy already running from `/Applications`. That final step used to live only in a checklist, and the menu bar once kept running a build six versions old. For a local install, run `scripts/install_local.sh`. It confirms the build exists, prints both versions, waits for the running app to exit, swaps the files, and verifies that the installed version matches. Buying a new light bulb is not the same as putting it in the socket. The script links removing the old bulb, fitting the new one, and checking that the light turns on, so the local copy actually catches up.

items.original: **`scripts/install_local.sh` replaces the hand-typed steps for installing a build locally.** Releasing does not touch `/Applications`: the tag drives CI, and the local copy keeps running whatever was already there. That last step lived only in a checklist, and the menu bar once ran a stale build for six versions before anyone noticed. The script checks the build exists, prints both versions, waits for the running app to exit, swaps it, and verifies the installed version matches.

entries: **The panel no longer creeps downward every time you open and close it.** Dragging it into place used to hold for one cycle at most: each reopen landed it a little lower than the last. Two anchors disagreed. The saved position was the window's bottom-left corner, but `setContentSizeKeepingTopLeft_` — added in 0.29.9 precisely so the panel would not appear to jump while resizing — holds the *top* edge. To hold that edge it calls `setFrameOrigin_`, and macOS posts `NSWindowDidMoveNotification` for a programmatic move just as it does for a drag, so `windowDidMove_` recorded a resize as though the user had dragged the window. Every open re-measured the content height, the bottom-left corner dropped by the difference, and that drop was saved as the new position. entries: **Removing the Codex status line no longer deletes one that `usage` never installed.** `_unsetup_codex()` only checked whether a `tui.status_line` existed at all, not whether it was ours. entries: **The report and the terminal's session list now show what each conversation was about.** Claude Code names every conversation and writes that name into its transcript. `usage` had been parsing those names all along and carrying them into the report payload, where the renderer ignored them — the snapshot fixture still read `"Ignore in current renderer"`. The card now reads "Reset imminent", in all five languages. title.zh-TW: 看不見的整理：選單列程式分家，尺寸規則自動把關
title.en: Invisible housekeeping: menu bar code gets divided up and size limits get enforced

body.zh-TW: 這版選單列畫面不變，整理藏在牆裡。`menubar.py` 已膨脹到 2,485 行，第三次超過 2,000 行。圖示與警示的輔助程式搬到 `menubar_chrome.py`，狀態建立程式移至 `menubar_state.py`，主檔降至 2,230 行。只移動檔案直屬函式。PyObjC（讓 Python 接上 macOS Objective-C 的橋樑）靠 `AppDelegate` 的方法名稱連接控制項，搬動它會令對應控制項失靈；`_popover_size` 則拆成計算函式，留三行外殼，讓無 ObjC 執行環境的單元測試仍能跑。接著，CI（自動檢查流程）開始替檔案尺寸守門，超限就讓建置失敗；切割檔案時降上限，別為通過檢查抬高它。CLAUDE.md 的模組地圖從 24 列縮到 12 列，只留會踩雷的說明。像整理屋內管線，表面不變，日後維修不必再越鑿越大。
body.en: Nothing new appears in the menu bar in this release; the work is behind the wall. `menubar.py` had grown to 2,485 lines and crossed 2,000 for the third time. Icon and alert helpers now live in `menubar_chrome.py`, while state constructors moved to `menubar_state.py`, bringing the original file down to 2,230 lines. Only file-level functions moved: PyObjC, the bridge between Python and macOS Objective-C, connects controls through `AppDelegate` method names, so moving one would silently break its control. `_popover_size` was split into a calculation function with a three-line shell left behind, keeping `menubar_state.py` testable without the ObjC runtime. CI, the automatic check run on changes, now fails a build when a guarded file exceeds its limit; after a cut, lower the limit rather than raising it to pass. CLAUDE.md's module map also shrank from 24 rows to 12, keeping only warnings that are not obvious from opening each module. It is like reorganizing plumbing: no new fixture appears, but later repairs need not keep breaking through a larger wall.

items.original:
**Nothing changes on screen in this release — it is housekeeping on the menu bar code.** `menubar.py` had reached 2485 lines, creeping past 2000 for the third time after being split apart twice. The icon and alert helpers moved into a new `menubar_chrome.py`, and the state constructors joined `menubar_state.py`, taking the file down to 2230. Only module-level functions moved: PyObjC binds `AppDelegate` methods by selector name, so relocating one would silently stop the matching control from working. `_popover_size` was split rather than moved, because it ends in `NSMakeSize` and `menubar_state.py` has to stay importable without the ObjC runtime for its projections to be unit-testable — the arithmetic moved as `popover_dimensions()` and a three-line shell stayed behind.
**The growth policy behind that cleanup is now enforced by CI rather than by discipline.** `scripts/check_file_size.py` fails the build when a guarded file passes its ceiling. The rule had been written in CLAUDE.md all along; nothing checked it, and the file grew back twice. Lower a ceiling when a cut lands, never raise it to go green.
**CLAUDE.md's module map lists only modules with a gotcha.** Half its rows restated what opening the file would tell you, and three separate rows repeated the same stdlib-only constraint. It went from 24 rows to 12.
